description: The Illinois Center for a Smarter Electric Grid keeps a page of publicly available, non-confidential power flow and transient stability cases. The page read on 2026-09-26 says every case includes a power flow and is offered in PowerWorld Simulator, Siemens PTI PSS/E and GE PSLF formats, with icons marking transient stability data, geomagnetic disturbance parameters, PowerWorld Dynamic Studio scenarios and case movies. Synthetic cases include a UIUC 150-bus system, Illinois200, Illini 42 cases for a tornado and a high-altitude electromagnetic pulse, South Carolina 500 and Texas 2000; literature cases include the Kundur two-area system, WSCC 9-bus, IEEE 14, 24, 30, 39, 57, 118 and 300-bus systems and the IEEE 96 RTS; and small signal stability benchmarks include the Brazilian seven-bus, New England 39 and 68-bus and a simplified Australian 14-generator system. Coverage is fictional and textbook networks, with no real utility data. Access is free download from the page; no licence is stated, and new cases can be contributed by email. Caveats: the synthetic cases are not real networks, and the formats need commercial or compatible tools. Simulation uses are power flow and stability studies, geomagnetic disturbance and extreme event resilience analysis. Related records: data-tamu-electric-grid-test-cases holds larger synthetic grids, and data-dr-power-egriddata-repository gathers test cases from several sources.
